title: Ammianus Marcellinus, Roman History 17.7.9-14 (English, C. D. Yonge, 1862)

source.license: Public domain (Yonge died 1891; Project Gutenberg text)

summary: Ammianus (4th century CE) on the causes of earthquakes. In 17.7.13 he says an island in the Atlantic was swallowed in a chasm-type quake, without naming Atlantis. A late-antique echo of the story.

tree.title: Ammianus Marcellinus 17.7.12-14: Anaximander on quakes; four kinds of earthquake and the Atlantic island
tree.summary: Ammianus gives Anaximander's theory of earthquakes, then four kinds. Under the gaping kind he lists the swallowing of a large island on the European coast of the Atlantic, Helice and Bura in the Gulf of Corinth, and the town of Saccumum in Italy.
